result.text:
Done. All 29 tests pass unchanged (`gradle test --rerun-tasks`, `tests="29" failures="0" errors="0"`), and `ImportTest.java` was not touched.

## What was wrong

- `importCustomer`: `if idType = "D" … else if "C" … else error`, with the DNI/CUIT validations inlined and `"Invalid CUIT number"` repeated five times.
- `importAddress`: the same shape, dispatching on whether the zip code starts with a digit or a letter.
- `Customer` / `Address`: type questions answered with `identificationType.equals("D")`, `zipCode instanceof Integer`, and `if/else` inside `dniNumberIfNone`, `cuitNumberIfNone`, `oldZipCodeIfNone`, `newZipCodeIfNone`.
- `chars().allMatch(Character::isDigit)` copied into every validation; the identification condition duplicated in both `CustomerSystem` subclasses.

## The design now

Two hierarchies replace the type codes:

- `Identification` (`src/main/java/customerimporter/Identification.java`) with `DNI` and `CUIT`. `Identification.forTypeAndNumber(type, number)` looks the creator up in a map keyed by each subclass's `TYPE` — an unknown type raises `"Invalid identification type"` via `orElseThrow`, no `if` — then sends `assertIsValid` to the new instance. `assertThat` is in the superclass and raises the subclass's `invalidNumberErrorDescription`, so each message exists once. `isDNI`/`isCUIT`/`dniNumberIfNone`/`cuitNumberIfNone` answer the "not of that type" case in the superclass and are overridden only by the class that owns them.
- `ZipCode` with `OldZipCode` and `NewZipCode`, same shape; `ZipCode.from` detects the first creator whose `appliesTo` holds (digit → old, letter → new).
- `Customer` holds an `Identification`, `Address` holds a `ZipCode`, and both keep the methods the tests use by delegating. `Customer.isIdentifiedBy` removed the condition repeated in `TransientCustomerSystem` and `PersistentCustomerSystem`.
- `CustomerImporter.importCustomer`/`importAddress` are now straight-line record-to-object code; `assertValidCustomerRecord` and `assertValidAddressRecord` share `assertRecordHasNumberOfFields`; `Characters.areAllDigits/areAllLetters` hold the repeated character checks.

## What I deliberately left

- The `if` on the record type in `importRecord` (`isCustomerRecord`/`isAddressRecord`) — it comes from the starting code, not from the new functionality.
- Two things the tests pin down: `Address.zipCode()` still answers an `Integer` or a `String` rather than the `ZipCode` object (`assertEquals(1001, importedAddress.zipCode())`), and a zip code that is neither old nor new still raises `"Invalid identification type"` — the copy-pasted message that `test29ZipCodeMustBeOldOrNew` asserts. It is now named `ZipCode.invalidZipCodeTypeErrorDescription()` with a comment saying why the text stays.

`README.md` described the old smelly design, so I updated it with a section on the design after the refactoring.
